{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=objective+misspecification+goal+criticism+reward+design+assumption+testing&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0010179600002859\", \"title\": [\"Robust Emergency Medical System Design as a Multi-objective Goal Programming Problem\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0010179600002859\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0010179600210028\", \"title\": [\"Robust Emergency Medical System Design as a Multi-objective Goal Programming Problem\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0010179600210028\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.3390/math13101593\", \"title\": [\"Robustness Study of Unit Elasticity of Intertemporal Substitution Assumption and Preference Misspecification\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper proposes a novel robustness framework for studying the unit elasticity of intertemporal substitution (EIS) assumption based on the Perron-Frobenius sieve estimation model by Christensen, 2017. The sieve nonparametric decomposition is a central model that connects key strands of the long run risk literature and recovers the stochastic discount factor (SDF) under the unit EIS assumption. I generate various economies based on Epstein–Zin preferences to simulate scenarios where the EIS deviates from unity. Then, I study the main estimation mechanism of the decomposition as well as the time discount factor and the risk aversion parameter estimation surface. The results demonstrate the robustness of estimating the average yield, change of measure, and preference parameters but also reveal an “absorption effect” arising from the unit EIS assumption. The findings highlight that asset pricing models assuming a unit EIS produce distorted parameter estimates, caution researchers about the potential under- or over-estimation of risk aversion, and provide insight into trends of misestimation when interpreting the results. I also identify an additional source of failure from a consumption component, which demonstrates a more general limit of the consumption-based capital asset pricing model and the structure used to estimate relevant preference parameters.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.3390/math13101593\", \"publish…

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=Bayesian+models+consensus+epistemic+disagreement+social+epistemology&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"William Wimsatt, Donald Campbell, and the Idea of Robustness.\", \"abstract\": \"In this paper, I chart the influence of social scientist Donald Campbell's work on William Wimsatt's ideas of robustness reasoning. One reason is that Campbell's work is less familiar in the broader philosophy of science literature. Another is that Wimsatt's famous 1981 paper on robustness was originally published in a Festschrift for Campbell and cited the three major works discussed here: on pattern-matching, on definitional operationism, and on the multitrait, multimethod matrix analysis of construct validity. I highlight some questions in contemporary debates in robustness reasoning: what is (are) the function(s) of robustness, the problem of discordant evidence, and the unification of robustness reasoning. I argue that some debates can be traced back to ideas present in both Campbell's and Wimsatt's work. Here I appeal to some unpublished notes and correspondence from Campbell as support and to coherence with Wimsatt's larger philosophical framework.
